q1: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, AVG(I.SALARY) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) INNER JOIN TEACHES AS T ON (C.COURSE_ID = T.COURSE_ID) INNER JOIN INSTRUCTOR AS I ON (D.DEPT_NAME = I.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING AVG(I.SALARY) > 50000 AND COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY) = 4

explanation: Q1 and Q2 differ in the condition for COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY). Q1 checks for exactly 4 distinct salaries, while Q2 checks for more than 4 distinct salaries. This difference can lead to different results if the number of distinct salaries in a department is 4 or more.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have a department with exactly 4 distinct instructor salaries to trigger a difference between Q1 and Q2. Any department with 4 or more distinct salaries will also trigger a difference, but the exact number is 4 for this counterexample.
